Deborah Williamson was appointed to serve as the director of the Kentucky Law-Related Education Program by Chief Justice Robert F. Stephen of the Kentucky Supreme Court in July 1991. In school systems, juvenile correction settings and community contexts, Ms. Williamson conducts law-related education awareness and training sessions, which highlight topics such as current research findings in the field, theoretical underpinnings, methodology and marshalling community support, for educators, law enforcement officers, juvenile justice practitioners and other community leaders. In addition, she has presented the Kentucky LRE model and research findings at the National Juvenile Detention Association Conference, the National Juvenile Justice Training Symposium, the American Bar Association's Youth for Citizenship Education Conference and the National Training and Dissemination's LRE in Juvenile Justice Settings Conference. Finally, Ms. Williamson is responsible for authoring grants to support LRE initiatives occurring throughout the state. Prior to her appointment as director of the state-wide project, Ms. Williamson served as an intake and diversion officer in the northern Kentucky area and as a field supervisor for the state's Court Designated Worker Program. Ms. Williamson holds an MA degree in cultural anthropology from the University of Cincinnati and is currently enrolled in the doctoral program at the University of Kentucky, Department of Sociology. Her area of interest is cognitive programming for juvenile offenders
